name: Luna 16
first: First robotic lunar sample return; first non-American lunar samples
description: Luna 16 was the Soviet Union's first successful robotic sample-return mission and the first non-crewed lunar return of any kind. After Apollo 11 brought home 22 kg of crewed samples in 1969, Luna 16 returned 101 grams of regolith from Mare Fecunditatis a year later — a fraction of Apollo's payload, but a profound proof-of-concept for the alternative architecture. The mission used a Proton-K booster and a direct return profile: descent to the surface, drill core, ascent stage launch, ballistic return capsule to Kazakhstan. The technique was reused for Luna 20 and Luna 24, and decades later by Chang'e 5 and Chang'e 6.
